To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HER 2/neur is a proto oncogene that is amplified and over expressed in a significant number of human breast and ovarian cancers, and that this amplification and overexpression is correlated with poor outcome in both diseases.
HER 2/neur is a candidate proto oncogene in breast and ovarian cancers.
HER 2/neulike amplification is a common event in human breast and ovary cancers, and is associated with poor clinical outcome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular alterations associated with the pathogenesis of breast and ovarian cancer and their role in the development and progression of these diseases.
identifying and characterizing genes that may be involved in carcinogenesis.
the identification and characterization of oncogenes in human cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HER 2/ne2 is a proto oncogene that is frequently altered in breast cancer and is also altered in some ovarian cancers and that the alteration is associated with poor prognosis.
HER 2/neul is a gene that is amplified in a large percentage of breast and ovarian tumors.
HER 2/ne u amplification and overexpression is a marker of a subset of breast and ovarian cancers with a poor prognosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HER 24/neu oncogene is amplified and over expressed in 20 percent of ovarian cancers.
HER 2/neus is amplified and over expressed in approximately 25% of breast and 30% of ovarian cancers.
the HER 3 gene is not amplified in breast or ovarian cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HER 2/neus involvement in ovarian and breast cancer is similar.
HER2 amplification is associated with poor outcome in breast and ovarian cancers, and that HER2 overexpression is also associated with poor outcome.
HER2 amplification and overexpression are associated with a worse outcome in both breast and ovarian cancers.
